title: MENA Clean Energy Market Outlook 2026 | BloombergNEF
gist: BNEF projects MENA solar and wind capacity to grow more than 8x from 49GW today to 404GW by 2035, with 2026 additions set to jump 37% as the Iran war reinforces the energy-security case for renewables and regional investors dominate a record $22 billion 2025 financing market.

insights.claim: BloombergNEF forecasts MENA's cumulative solar and wind capacity to reach 404GW by 2035, up from 49GW today, implying roughly an 8x expansion over the decade.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Signals a decade-long structural buildout in Gulf and North African power markets, favoring developers, EPC contractors and equipment suppliers with regional exposure.
insights.quote: 404GW: Projected 2035 cumulative solar and wind capacity in MENA, up from 49GW today

insights.claim: MENA installed a record 16 gigawatts of solar and wind capacity in 2025, and total additions are set to rise 37% in 2026.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: A 37% year-on-year acceleration indicates the region is still in the steep part of its renewables adoption curve, not plateauing.

insights.claim: Solar remains the primary driver of MENA clean power growth, with additions projected to hit a record 18GW in 2026, dominated by utility-scale projects under expanding government-led procurement programs.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Government procurement (tenders/PPAs) rather than merchant or distributed solar is the primary demand driver, favoring large developers able to win sovereign-backed auctions.

insights.claim: Solar deployment in MENA is broadening geographically, with five markets each exceeding 1GW of installations in 2026.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Diversification beyond a handful of leading markets reduces single-country concentration risk for regional investors and suppliers.

themes.theme: Iran war as a geopolitical accelerant for renewables

insights.claim: The Iran war has heightened MENA governments' concerns over energy security and fossil fuel exposure, strengthening the strategic case for renewables.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: A live regional conflict is being used by BNEF as a causal driver of accelerated clean-energy policy, a factor investors should track alongside oil price shocks when weighing MENA renewables exposure.

insights.claim: For oil- and gas-producing MENA countries, renewables deployment is framed as a way to free up more hydrocarbons for export rather than domestic power burn.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: This 'freed-up export barrels' logic ties renewables buildout directly to producer-country export revenue and oil market supply, relevant for energy investors modeling OPEC+ producers' spare capacity.

insights.claim: For MENA countries that import energy, renewables deployment is framed as reducing import dependence, a distinct rationale from that of exporting nations.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: The dual rationale (export-freeing for producers, import-substitution for importers) suggests renewables policy support is broad-based across the region regardless of a country's hydrocarbon endowment.

themes.theme: Wind and storage entering scale-up phase

insights.claim: Wind deployment in MENA is far more geographically concentrated than solar, with Egypt and Saudi Arabia together accounting for 86% of forecast wind additions over 2026-2035.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Wind investment opportunity in MENA is effectively a two-country bet on Egypt and Saudi Arabia for the next decade, unlike the more diversified solar market.
insights.quote: Wind deployment remains more concentrated than solar, with Egypt and Saudi Arabia accounting for 86% of forecast additions over 2026- 2035.

insights.claim: Battery storage capacity additions in MENA are forecast to reach 4GW/16GWh in 2026, double the prior year's capacity, scaling through both co-located projects and a growing pipeline of standalone battery storage auctions.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: A doubling of storage additions and the emergence of standalone (not just co-located) battery auctions signals MENA storage is moving from a nascent, solar-attached add-on to an independent asset class investors can underwrite directly.
insights.quote: 4GW/16GWh: Forecast battery capacity additions in MENA in 2026, double last year’s capacity

themes.theme: Record investment and the rise of regional capital

insights.claim: MENA renewable energy investment reached $22 billion in 2025, marking a third consecutive annual record.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Three straight record years indicates sustained, not one-off, capital inflow momentum into MENA clean power, a positive signal for financiers and equipment suppliers assessing deal flow durability.
insights.quote: $22 billion: Renewable energy investment in MENA in 2025, a third consecutive annual record

insights.claim: Regional investors accounted for 85% of MENA renewable energy financing activity in 2025, indicating the market is increasingly self-funded rather than reliant on international capital.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: An 85% regional-investor share suggests global funds face a narrowing entry window and that Gulf sovereign wealth and regional banks are becoming the dominant price-setters in MENA clean energy deals.
insights.quote: regional investors accounted for 85% of 2025 financing activity

insights.claim: BNEF's forecasts in this outlook are built on its proprietary wind, solar and storage assets database, incorporating country targets, regional economics and electricity demand growth as inputs.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Clarifies the forecast methodology (bottom-up asset database plus policy targets and demand growth), useful context for weighing how much confidence to place in the 404GW 2035 figure.
